decided.singular: These are the narrow spikes that reach about 6.5 to 8.7 above a background that mostly sits between 1 and 5. The largest are near day 316 (about 8.7), day 1 (about 8), and days 106 and 152 (about 7.7).
decided.recurrence: There are some hints of spacing between peaks (for example 246, 258 and 272), but I could not see a regular 20 to 35 day train of bursts across the year that I could tell apart from noise.
decided.quarter: Q2 has two of the major spikes (106 and 152-154) plus the cluster around 164, on a fairly high baseline. Q4 has the single largest spike but a similar baseline, and Q3 (days 210-250) is visibly the quietest, so the choice between Q2 and Q4 was close.

answer.guess: A 3-hourly geomagnetic activity index such as Kp (0-9 scale, eight values per day).
